dataset: Shelters reported as used in Mae Sai district during the September 2024 flood
compiled_by: FloodGuard desk research (Thai and English news, PRD/ICC situation reports, OSM/Nominatim for locations)
status: Reported use from public sources; not an official register. Locations are OSM matches where possible; low-confidence locations are approximate.
licence_note: Facts with citations; OSM-derived coordinates © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
caveats:
1) Which flood each source describes. Mae Sai flooded repeatedly: 10-13 Sep 2024 (the main event), again in early Oct 2024, then May 2025 and July 2025. Several search hits look like Sep 2024 but are not. Thai PBS World 'Four communities evacuated', The Nation 40050383 and 40053207, Bangkok Post 3076938 and Khaosod 9869431 are all from May or July 2025, so I excluded them as evidence for Sep 2024. They only suggest a recurring shelter set: municipality office, Wat Phrom Wihan, Municipal School 1 and the district hall. The Oct 2024 numbers (8-10 Oct) are included only as context for continued use.

2) Where the site list comes from. The 17-site list comes from the Chiang Rai Incident Command Center (ศูนย์บัญชาการเหตุการณ์) report covering 9-15 Sep 2024. It is dated about 15 Sep 2024 and says 17 sites held 1,343 people. The 21 Sep list has 6 sites and 501 people; the 28 Sep list has 3 sites and 237 people. I read these through two media outlets that republished the ICC text: FM91 and nakornchiangrainews, which credits the Chiang Rai PR Office. I could not locate the original September pages on chiangrai.prd.go.th. The 10 Oct report on chiangrai.prd.go.th is official. A 24 Sep ICC report exists (chiangraifocus 33610) but returned 403, so it was not read.

3) Sources I could not read. thaigov.go.th pages returned a Cloudflare challenge, which I did not bypass. Thairath returned 403. WebFetch returned 403 for Matichon, but a plain curl read worked.

4) Occupancy numbers. These are point-in-time 'remaining' (คงค้าง) counts, not capacities. The first-night figures (34 at the municipality, 37 at Wat Phrom Wihan, as of 11 Sep 01:00) come before the 11-12 Sep peak. The peak occupancy count I found is the 9-15 Sep list (1,343 people across 17 sites); the lists run about 15 Sep, then 21 Sep, then 28 Sep. The shelters outside the town (Ko Chang, Pong Pha, Si Mueang Chum, Pong Ngam) only appear on that list and had closed by 21 Sep. No capacity figures were published for Sep 2024, except MSDHS's 50 for Baan Ua-Arthorn.

5) Tambon labels. Nominatim/OSM admin tags in this area mix municipalities and tambons and are unreliable. For example, Wat Mongkhon Thammakayaram is labelled แม่ไร่ (Mae Chan) although registries say ต.โป่งงาม, อ.แม่สาย. Tambon values here come from official or registry text where available.

6) Locations. OSM coverage is good for the town-centre sites: municipality office, Wat Phrom Wihan, Wat Tham Pha Chom, Wat Mueang Daeng, district office, Wat Nam Cham, Wat Chetiyaram, and the Wat Mongkhon buildings. OSM IDs were verified via Overpass (OSM base timestamp 2026-09-27T11:07Z). Coverage is poor for the eastern Ko Chang temples: Wat Pa Sang Ngam, Wat Pa Daeng and Wat San Luang have no named OSM feature. Low-confidence points are village nodes or non-OSM listings and need proper geocoding before any access analysis. Overpass rate-limited several requests (about 429s), so not every alternative spelling was tried.

7) Relief sites that are not overnight shelters. The Mae Sai District Office was the incident command centre and hosted kitchens. The Pornpairin Apartment (Pa Muead Soi 2) offered free rooms to outside responders and free parking to flood victims (Matichon/Thai PBS, 11 Sep). It was not an evacuee shelter, so it is excluded. The Chiang Rai United stadium and the Chiang Rai PAO (อบจ.) school shelters from the same 11 Sep list are in Mueang Chiang Rai, not Mae Sai, and are excluded.

8) Site-specific uncertainties. Wat Mueang Daeng was itself flooded and evacuated at the peak (DDPM, 12 Sep) and only became a shelter later, which matters for a day-by-day replay. The ICC lines 'วัดเจติยาราม' and 'วัดสันธาตุ' are probably one temple (my inference). The unnamed 15 Sep 'church' may or may not be the Ban Pha Hi church named on 21 Sep.

9) What was not done. No data files were downloaded or saved and nothing was written to the repo. Two small helper scripts and temporary Overpass query text files were written only to the session scratchpad.

A second Wat Chetiyaram exists at Ban San Na, Moo 8, ต.เกาะช้าง, so the identification is not certain.

shelters.name_en: Baan Ua-Arthorn Mae Sai 1 housing project shelter (Ministry of Social Development and Human Security, MSDHS)
shelters.address_or_area: โครงการบ้านเอื้ออาทรจังหวัดเชียงราย (แม่สาย 1), ต.โป่งผา
shelters.location_evidence: The coordinates come from the Baania real-estate project page for 'บ้านเอื้ออาทรจังหวัดเชียงราย (แม่สาย 1)', a commercial listing I did not verify. Nominatim reverse at this point returns the road 'ถนนบ้านน้ำจำ-บ้านสันโค้ง' (way 93038659). There is no OSM landuse or named feature for the project.
shelters.period_used: MSDHS had prepared it as a shelter by 2024-09-14 (capacity 50). It housed 17 people on 2024-09-21 and is not listed on 2024-09-28.
shelters.reported_capacity_or_occupancy: Capacity 50 (MSDHS, 2024-09-14). Occupancy 17 (2024-09-21). MSDHS also prepared 'แม่สาย 2' (capacity 50), but I found no occupancy reported for it.
shelters.notes: This was a shelter for vulnerable groups (elderly, disabled, children). The location is weak, so geocode it properly before use.
